summary: Prednisolone is a systemic glucocorticoid used across endocrine, rheumatic, collagen, dermatologic, allergic, ophthalmic, respiratory, haematologic, neoplastic, oedematous and gastrointestinal disorders. Dosage is highly individualised (5-60 mg/day initially) and should be tapered. Long-term use causes HPA-axis suppression and corticosteroid adverse effects.
indications: Endocrine disorders (e.g. adrenocortical insufficiency, congenital adrenal hyperplasia, hypercalcaemia of malignancy)
Rheumatic disorders (e.g. rheumatoid arthritis, acute gout, bursitis) as adjunctive short-term therapy
Collagen diseases (e.g. systemic lupus erythematosus, acute rheumatic carditis)
Dermatologic diseases (e.g. pemphigus, severe erythema multiforme, severe psoriasis)
Allergic states (severe or incapacitating, intractable to conventional treatment)
Ophthalmic, respiratory, haematologic, neoplastic, oedematous and gastrointestinal disorders

dosage.d: Initial 5-60 mg/day depending on disease severity
dosage.n: Individualise; reduce gradually to lowest effective dose

dosage.d: Decrease in small increments to lowest dose maintaining response
dosage.n: Stress doses may be needed during illness/surgery

dosage.d: Based on disease and body weight rather than strict age formula

admin: Take with food to reduce gastric irritation
Give as a single morning dose where possible to mimic circadian rhythm
Do not stop abruptly after prolonged use - taper to avoid adrenal insufficiency
Increase dose during physiologic stress (infection, surgery, trauma)
moa: Prednisolone diffuses into cells and binds cytoplasmic glucocorticoid receptors; the complex modulates gene transcription to suppress inflammatory mediators (cytokines, prostaglandins, leukotrienes), reduce capillary permeability and leukocyte migration, and produce broad immunosuppressive effects.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to prednisolone or components
Administration of live or live-attenuated vaccines at immunosuppressive doses

preg: Corticosteroids cross the placenta; some animal data show teratogenicity (cleft palate) and human use is associated with intrauterine growth restriction. Use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the risk; observe infants of mothers on substantial doses for adrenal insufficiency.
lact: Corticosteroids are excreted in human milk and could suppress growth or endogenous steroid production at high doses. Low maternal doses are generally considered compatible; monitor the infant.
renal: No specific dose adjustment; monitor fluid retention, electrolytes and blood pressure.
hepatic: Prednisolone is the active moiety (unlike prednisone, which needs hepatic conversion); it can be used in hepatic impairment but with monitoring for fluid retention and infection.

major: Live vaccines - risk of disseminated infection at immunosuppressive doses
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. ketoconazole, ritonavir) - increase corticosteroid exposure
moderate: CYP3A4 inducers (rifampin, phenytoin, phenobarbital) - reduce corticosteroid effect
interactions.food: Take with food; high-salt diet worsens fluid retention
interactions.alcohol: Increases risk of GI ulceration and bleeding
interactions.diagnostics: Can suppress reactions to skin tests; affects ACTH/cortisol testing; raises glucose

serious: HPA-axis suppression / adrenal insufficiency on withdrawal

monitoring: Bone mineral density with long-term use
Signs of infection and growth in children
counsel: Take with food, ideally in the morning
Never stop suddenly after prolonged use - the dose must be reduced gradually
Carry a steroid card; you may need higher doses when ill or before surgery
Report signs of infection, severe stomach pain, black stools or mood changes
Avoid live vaccines and tell providers you take a steroid
pk: Plasma Tmax 1-2 hours after oral dosing
Store at controlled room temperature, protect from light
pearls: Active form - no hepatic activation needed (preferred over prednisone in liver disease)
Always taper after prolonged courses to avoid adrenal crisis
Provide stress-dose cover during illness or surgery
Monitor glucose, BP, bone density and for infection on long-term therapy
Single morning dosing reduces HPA-axis suppression
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is nearly time for the next dose, skip it - do not double up. Do not stop the medicine without medical advice.
overdose: Acute overdose rarely causes serious harm. Chronic excess produces Cushingoid features, hyperglycaemia, hypertension, hypokalaemia and immunosuppression. Manage supportively; do not stop abruptly if dependent. Treat metabolic effects as indicated.
